strategy_title: Direct K-major B load without tl.trans() worsened bank conflicts
strategy_description: Loading the B matrix directly in [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] layout (k*stride_bk + n*stride_bn) to call tl.dot(a, b) without tl.trans() — intended to eliminate shared memory bank conflicts — instead caused a 1.6x regression. Bank conflicts worsened from 11.9-way to 16.8-way, excess shared load wavefronts grew from 74% to 80%, and MIO stall fraction rose from 60.5% to 83.1% of cycles, tripling Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction (4.77→14.3). Although registers/thread dropped (128→80) and achieved occupancy doubled (6.24%→12.48%), the increased stall rate per warp more than offset any occupancy gain. This is the third consecutive iteration producing the same ~0.62x regression pattern: changing the B-load layout + autotuning only num_warps/num_stages (without varying tile sizes BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K as constexpr autotune parameters) consistently amplifies bank conflicts and MIO stalls for this kernel's fixed tile geometry.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: TMA block pointer loads, block_size=128, BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32
A_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=A, shape=(M,K), strides=(stride_am,stride_ak), ...)
B_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=B, shape=(K,N), strides=(stride_bk,stride_bn), ...)
for k_idx in range(tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    b = tl.load(B_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# After: manual pointer arithmetic [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] B load, autotune num_warps/num_stages only, block_size=256
# BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K still fixed — tile sizes NOT autotuned
for k_idx in range(tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    offs_k_iter = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K) + k_idx * BLOCK_K
    a_ptrs = A + offs_a_m[:, None] * 160 + offs_k_iter[None, :]
    a = tl.load(a_ptrs)
    b_ptrs = B + offs_k_iter[:, None] * 1 + offs_b_n[None, :] * 160  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
    b = tl.load(b_ptrs)
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
# @triton.autotune only sweeps num_warps in {2,4,8}, num_stages in {2,3,4}
applicable_when: Never — this combination consistently causes ~0.62x regression across iterations 2, 3, and 4. Any B-load layout change without simultaneously varying BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K as constexpr autotune parameters fails to resolve the structural bank conflict pattern.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply any B-matrix load layout change (whether [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K]+tl.trans() or direct [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]) combined with autotune that only sweeps num_warps/num_stages when tile sizes are fixed at BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32. Three consecutive iterations (2, 3, 4) with different B-load strategies all produced the same ~0.62x regression: bank conflicts worsen from ~12-way to ~17-way, MIO stall fraction rises from ~61% to ~83%, and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction triples. The root fix requires exposing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K as constexpr autotune parameters to change the fundamental shared memory access pattern.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune configs must include BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K as tl.constexpr kernel parameters and pass them in the Config dict for tile-size autotuning to take effect. Sweeping only num_warps/num_stages without tile size variation does not change the shared memory bank conflict pattern. Switching from tl.make_block_ptr/tl.advance to manual pointer arithmetic also does not resolve bank conflicts when tile dimensions are unchanged.

strategy_title: Removing tl.trans() worsened bank conflicts and MIO stalls
strategy_description: Replacing a transposed B-matrix load (tl.load of [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] + tl.trans()) with a natural [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] strided pointer load — while simultaneously adding @triton.autotune over num_warps/num_stages and doubling block size from 128 to 256 threads — caused a 1.6x regression. Despite registers/thread dropping from 128 to 80 and achieved occupancy doubling (6.24%→12.48%), shared memory bank conflicts worsened from 11.9-way to 16.8-way, MIO stall fraction rose from 60.5% to 83.1% of cycles, and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction tripled (4.77→14.29). The confounding factor is that doubling block size with fixed tile dimensions (BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32) amplified the bank conflict pattern — the same failure mode observed in iteration 2 (item b7c3f91e). Changing the B-load access pattern alone does not resolve bank conflicts when tile sizes and block size are simultaneously changed in ways that worsen the shared memory stride pattern.
slow_pseudocode:
# Before: TMA block pointer loads, block_size=128, 128 regs/thread
A_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=A, shape=(M,K), strides=(stride_am,stride_ak), ...)
B_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=B, shape=(K,N), strides=(stride_bk,stride_bn), ...)
for k_idx in range(tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    b = tl.load(B_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# After: manual pointer arithmetic, block_size=256, 80 regs/thread, autotune num_warps/num_stages
# BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K still fixed at 64/64/32
for k_idx in range(tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    offs_k_iter = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K) + k_idx * BLOCK_K
    a_ptrs = A + offs_a_m[:, None] * 160 + offs_k_iter[None, :]
    a = tl.load(a_ptrs)
    b_ptrs = B + offs_k_iter[:, None] * 1 + offs_b_n[None, :] * 160  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
    b = tl.load(b_ptrs)
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)  # no tl.trans()
applicable_when: Never — this combination caused regression. The natural [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] B-load pointer arithmetic may be correct in isolation, but combined with doubling block size and autotuning only num_warps/num_stages (not tile sizes), it amplifies bank conflicts.
do_not_apply_when: Do not attempt to fix shared memory bank conflicts by changing B-matrix load layout (removing tl.trans or switching from block_ptr to manual pointer arithmetic) while simultaneously increasing block size with fixed tile dimensions. When BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K are not exposed as autotuned constexpr parameters, changing block size with fixed tiles amplifies bank conflict patterns rather than resolving them. This is the second iteration (items b7c3f91e and a9f2b3c1) confirming that autotuning only num_warps/num_stages without tile size variation causes regression in this kernel.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.make_block_ptr with natural strides (stride_bk, stride_bn) is equivalent to manual pointer arithmetic b_ptrs = B + k[:, None]*stride_bk + n[None,:]*stride_bn. Neither approach resolves bank conflicts when the tile dimensions create stride patterns that alias to the same shared memory banks. The fix requires changing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K as constexpr autotune parameters, not just the load mechanism.
